title: Shell and fan triangle shawl
subtitle: Top-down triangle shawl in DK with a 5-treble fan separated by ch-1 spaces on a 4 mm hook
excerpt: A top-down triangular shawl worked entirely in a 5-treble fan stitch set in ch-2 corner spaces, separated by single chain stitches. The shawl grows from a short chain spine at the neck to a full triangle 150 cm wide and 72 cm deep. The fan repeat is two rows: a fan row and a chain-space return row.
sourceNotes: Shell and fan stitch construction from Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 1 (1886), which describes fan-stitch shawls worked from a central neck chain with increasing fan widths per row (Internet Archive). Fan stitch construction also in Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886).
heroPrompt: A triangular crochet shawl in soft sage green DK cotton pinned flat on a blocking mat. The open fan stitches along both diagonal edges and across the body are clearly visible from above.

crochet.gaugeText: 1 fan (5 tr) + 1 ch-1 space = 3 cm wide. 2 rows (1 fan row + 1 return row) = 2.5 cm tall. Approximately 10 cm per 3-4 fan-and-space repeats in DK on a 4 mm hook.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approximately 150 cm wide x 72 cm deep at the centre, blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: Five treble stitches worked into the same chain space or stitch, spreading out at the top to form a fan shape. In this pattern each fan sits in a ch-2 corner space with ch-1 spaces separating fans on either side.

The central foundation chain from which a top-down triangular shawl grows. Stitches are worked on both sides of the spine; the spine is marked with a stitch marker and the marker moves up on each row.

content.text: This triangular shawl starts from a short
spine chain
at the neck and grows downward by adding one
fan stitch

on each side of the spine on every fan row. The construction is top-down, worked flat in rows and turned at each edge. The ch-1 turning chain does not count as a stitch. The repeat is two rows: a fan row, where you work 5-treble fans into the ch-2 spaces of the previous row; and a return row, where you work dc and ch spaces across to set up the next fan row.

The fan stitch is accessible to beginners who are confident with treble crochet, chaining, and basic counting. The main skill to practise is placing each fan accurately in the correct ch-2 space. Stitch markers are essential at the spine chain position and at the two edge fan positions.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Approximately 400 g DK-weight yarn (cotton or cotton-blend gives good stitch definition in the open fan repeat). A 4 mm hook (US G/6). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Stitch markers (3 minimum). Blocking mat and pins. Tape measure.

content.text: Gauge

1 fan (5 tr) + 1 ch-1 space measures 3 cm wide; 2 rows (fan row + return row) measure 2.5 cm tall in DK on a 4 mm hook. Work a swatch of 5 fans across for 6 rows (3 fan rows + 3 return rows), block it, and measure. At gauge, 5 fans should measure 15 cm wide and 6 rows should measure 7.5 cm tall.
Stitches used
ch: chain -- UK and US shared.
sl st: slip stitch -- UK and US shared.
dc: double crochet (UK) -- used on return rows. The same move as US single crochet (sc).
tr: treble (UK) -- the main stitch of the fan. The same move as US double crochet (dc).
Fan stitch
: 5 tr in the same ch-2 space.
Pattern
The shawl is worked flat, turning at the end of each row. Mark the spine chain at the centre with a stitch marker. Move the marker up each row.
Foundation
Ch 5. Mark the 3rd ch from the hook with a stitch marker. This is the spine position.
Row 1 (right side, set-up)
Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). 1 dc in first ch. Ch 2. 1 dc in marked spine ch (move marker to this dc). Ch 2. 1 dc in last ch. Turn. (3 dc, 2 ch-2 spaces)
Row 2 (wrong side, return row)
Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). 1 dc in first dc. Ch 2. 1 dc in spine dc (move marker). Ch 2. 1 dc in last dc. Turn. (3 dc, 2 ch-2 spaces)
Row 3 (right side, first fan row)

Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). 1 dc in first dc. Ch 1. 5 tr in first ch-2 space (first fan). Ch 2. 5 tr in second ch-2 space (second fan). Ch 1. 1 dc in last dc. Turn. (2 fans, 2 ch-2 spaces, 2 edge dc)
Row 4 (wrong side, return row)

Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). 1 dc in first dc. Ch 2. 1 dc in ch-1 space between fan and centre. Ch 2 (spine position -- move marker to this dc). 1 dc in ch-1 space between centre and second fan. Ch 2. 1 dc in last dc. Turn. (4 dc, 3 ch-2 spaces)
Row 5 (right side, fan row, 3 fans)
Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). 1 dc in first dc. Ch 1. *5 tr in next ch-2 space. Ch 1.* Repeat from * to * twice more (3 fans total). 1 dc in last dc. Turn. (3 fans, 3 ch-1 separators, 2 edge dc)
Rows 6 onwards -- increase pattern

Continue the two-row repeat: on every return row (even rows), work dc in each gap between fans with ch-2 between, adding a ch-2 space at both edges; on every fan row (odd rows), work 5 tr in each ch-2 space with ch-1 between, and dc at each edge. Each fan row adds two fans to the total count (one per side of the spine). Work until you have 25 fans across on the fan row (approximately 57 rows total). The shawl should measure 150 cm wide at this row. (25 fans)
Final return row
Work the final return row after the 25-fan row to set the last row of ch-2 spaces. Fasten off. The total depth from the neck to the lower point is approximately 72 cm.
Finishing

Fasten off and weave in all ends. Wet-block by soaking in cool water for 10 minutes, pressing water out gently in a towel, then pinning to the stated dimensions on a blocking mat. Pin the two top corners first, then pin the point at the base, then pin the two diagonal edges at 10 cm intervals.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild soap. Do not tumble-dry. Lay flat and ease to shape while damp. DK cotton holds its block well; wool-blend yarn may need re-pinning after the first wash.
What to try next

A 7-treble fan in the same construction produces a more dramatic open arc shape. Working the same fan repeat in a lace-weight yarn on a 3 mm hook produces a fine summer shawlette in far fewer grams. Adding a picot border along the lower diagonal edges (ch 3, sl st in base of ch 3) gives the fan edge a decorative finish.
